items.title: Frank Goudie Interview
items.q: I've lost a job in Brechtop on the Carlos Sidney Baxter... I found out that Brechtop wanted to get rid of me to take him.

ctx.x: Well, the, the horn practically blew up in his hands, so. Great man. Uh, you were telling me when you were over there, let's see, this would be, uh, oh, a long time later, uh, that, uh, I always got the impression when I hear him that, my God, he frightened you to death to be in the same room with him. Is that so? To you?

Did you ever get that impression? Of, uh, of Sidney? Yeah. Well, Sidney, I knew Sidney since, uh, I think 27 or 29, when he left Germany to go back to France. He was in Germany at that time. And I, I've lost a job in Brechtop on the Carlos Sidney Baxter. When Baxter came from Germany, jazz had changed in Germany, you see, and as he, as he couldn't read, he got it sort of hard because he couldn't change his style, didn't know the Martin Nogues that was coming out. And so he had it at the time kind of hard, became…
